what: Diamondback Energy is a pure Permian basin oil producer in West Texas. It drills and operates wells, and after buying Endeavor Energy it is one of the largest holders of Permian acreage.
customers: Refiners and crude buyers, mostly along the US Gulf Coast.
money: Oil, natural gas and natural gas liquids
gathering infrastructure and mineral interests through Viper Energy
moat: Contiguous Permian acreage with low drilling costs per barrel and decades of inventory, in the basin with the best economics in North America.
risks: Debt of about $13 billion rose with the Endeavor acquisition
Oil prices set earnings and it does not hedge much of its production
Return on invested capital of about 2% reflects the acquisition's cost base
Shale wells decline quickly, so drilling must continue just to hold production
opportunities: Revenue grew about 36% last year as acquired production was added
Among the lowest costs per barrel of any US shale producer
Analysts see about 35% upside from current levels
watch: Cost per well, free cash flow, and the pace of debt reduction.
